$comment: The curated half of the DOM binding: what AngleSharp's attributes cannot say. Every entry carries a
reason, and every entry has to name something the pinned assemblies actually have — DomBindingsOverrideTests
fails on one that does not, so this table can never quietly describe a version of AngleSharp nobody
references any more. Members left out for a reason the generator worked out for itself (a Task-returning
member, a delegate parameter, a type the conversion table has no entry for) are NOT listed here: they are
in the generated report, with the reason the generator gave.

excludedInterfaces.reason: DOM merged DOMSettableTokenList into DOMTokenList in 2016 and the interface no longer exists; AngleSharp still carries [DomName("DOMSettableTokenList")] on ISettableTokenList, so `iframe.sandbox`, `output.htmlFor` and `link.sizes` were projected onto an interface no standard declares -- `Object.prototype.toString.call(iframe.sandbox)` read `[object DOMSettableTokenList]`. Excluding it makes DomTypeMap fall through to ITokenList, which is DOMTokenList, and takes the interface object off the global with it. Its one member was already skipped: ISettableTokenList.Value answers the SERIALIZED token set where DOM's `value` is the attribute verbatim, and the inherited DOMTokenList.value is the standard's.

Window is the browser runtime's, not the binding's: the global object stays Jint's GlobalObject and gains Window.prototype in its chain (campaign item R1). Generating a second Window here would produce an interface object nothing could ever be an instance of. document.defaultView is skipped with it, by the conversion table rather than by name.

Touch is the events bridge's, for the reason every other event interface is: no type in either pinned assembly implements ITouchPoint, so nothing could ever produce one and the generated interface object was an unreachable shell. It also carries only eight of Touch Events Level 2's twelve members - radiusX, radiusY, rotationAngle and force are absent - and its Target is an IEventTarget this package wraps rather than owns. Jint.Browser/Events/TouchInterfaces.cs declares the whole interface, with the constructor WebIDL gives it. Recorded in Jint.Browser/Dom/divergences.md.

TouchList goes with Touch: nothing implements it either, and a list of an interface the binding no longer projects has nothing to hold. Declared beside it in Jint.Browser/Events/TouchInterfaces.cs, over the same ArrayLikeObject lane the generated collections use.

HTML has no HTMLTableDataCellElement: it was merged into HTMLTableCellElement and html/dom/historical.html asserts the interface is gone from the window. AngleSharp splits the interface in two, which put a name on the global that no standard declares and gave <td> a prototype chain one link too long. Its shape carried no members of its own, so excluding it costs nothing; <td> is an HTMLTableCellElement now, which is also what the HTMLElement constructor's interface check wanted. Recorded in Jint.Browser/Dom/divergences.md.

The other half of the same split, and the same removed name. Its one member, scope, is HTMLTableCellElement's in HTML, so it comes back as a reflected row on that interface rather than being lost with the interface.

manual.reason: AngleSharp's IHtmlCollection<T> is generic and invariant, so a static member body cannot name the receiver type. item() and namedItem() are hand-written against DomCollectionBase's two virtuals instead, and the interface contributes no members to any closure — its refinements inherit them through the prototype chain, which is where a browser has them too.

HTML §4.13.2.3 declares HTMLAllCollection as a standalone interface whose length, item(nameOrIndex) and namedItem(name) are its own, whose named lookup answers an element or an HTMLCollection, and which carries a legacy caller and ECMAScript Annex B.3.6's [[IsHTMLDDA]] slot. AngleSharp models it as IHtmlAllCollection : IHtmlCollection<IElement>, which is the one place the CLR hierarchy contradicts the IDL: `inherits: ""` roots the prototype at Object.prototype the way HTML does rather than at HTMLCollection, and `wrapper` selects the hand-written DomHtmlAllCollectionObject over the generic collection wrapper, which could carry neither the legacy caller nor the slot.

skip.reason: HTML's `add((HTMLOptionElement or HTMLOptGroupElement) element, ...)` is a union, and AngleSharp models it as two AddOption overloads sharing one [DomName]. The generator binds one member per name, so one half would always lose; re-declared in `additions` over a body that dispatches on the argument's interface.

HTML §2.5.3 gives every element including HTMLOrSVGElement a nonce whose setter writes the [[CryptographicNonce]] slot and NOT the content attribute, which is what keeps a header-delivered policy's nonce out of a CSS selector. The reflected scrollAmount row replaces it.

AngleSharp has no [DomName] for it at all, so nothing could generate it -- and it is not a corner: a library asks it to tell a node in the document from one in a shadow tree or in a detached fragment, and Playwright's injected script calls it on every element it touches.

AngleSharp has no member of that name at all -- its [DomName("charset")] members are HTMLAnchorElement's and HTMLScriptElement's content attributes -- so the alias has to be declared here.

DOM §4.5.1. AngleSharp's IImplementation is createHTMLDocument, createDocumentType and hasFeature, and nothing else, so there is nothing to project; the algorithm is DOM's own over the pieces AngleSharp does have.

DOM §6.1. AngleSharp has it, but its third parameter is a NodeFilter delegate and the conversion table has no entry for a delegate — deliberately, because only the standard knows a callback's IDL shape. Dom/Views/NodeFilters accepts both shapes DOM's legacy callback interface allows.

CSSOM View extends Range with it and AngleSharp has no layout to answer from. Zeros, honestly, until the flat-box model (campaign item C4) gives every box a deterministic rectangle.
The other half of getBoundingClientRect: an empty list, because a range with no layout covers no boxes.
